name: alert
description: A message in a hue: a tinted box with a colored edge, an optional icon, and an optional close button that the module wires up.

attributes.name: data-variant
attributes.description: Which hue: success for done, warning for careful, danger for wrong (alert is the same ladder under its Foundation 6 name), primary for news.

attributes.name: data-emphasis
attributes.description: How loud: medium is a tint, high a solid fill, low the border alone.

children.description: An icon, first, sized to the text.
A button, last, that removes the alert when alert.js is loaded.

markers.name: data-close
markers.description: The close button; removes the alert when alert.js is loaded.

tokens.name: --yeti-alert-edge
tokens.description: Width of the start edge, at every emphasis. Undeclared; falls back to four times the local --yeti-border-width.

tokens.name: --yeti-border-width
tokens.description: The border on every side but the start edge.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-sm
tokens.description: Gap between the icon, the body, and the close button.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-primary
tokens.description: The default variant's color, when data-variant is absent.

tokens.name: --yeti-on-primary
tokens.description: Text on the default variant's color.

tokens.name: --yeti-duration-fast
tokens.description: How long the alert takes to fade out when alert.js dismisses it.

keyboard.action: On the close button, removes the alert.

a11y.notes: Use role="status" for the usual notice, which is announced politely, and role="alert" only for something urgent, which interrupts. Content present at page load is not announced by either role; the roles matter for alerts inserted later. Meaning carried by the color must also be in the words. The close button needs a name. Without the module the button does nothing, so leave it out on pages that do not load alert.js.

events.name: yeti:close
events.description: Dispatched on the .alert after the fade and before it is removed, while it is still in the page.
